description: Distributed systems as graph-resident theory. Beyond what databases_and_storage covers (consensus, replication, CAP, sharding): microservices architecture, service mesh, resilience patterns (circuit breaker, bulkhead, retry+backoff), saga/event-sourcing/CQRS, distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), service discovery, load balancing, distributed transactions (2PC, TCC), logical time (Lamport, vector, hybrid), failure detection (heartbeat, gossip, phi accrual), idempotency, delivery semantics (at-most/at-least/exactly-once), rate limiting, distributed locking, chaos engineering, SRE (SLA/SLO/SLI/error budgets), observability. The mechanisms by which independent processes cooperate at scale despite network unreliability.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory + databases_and_storage + network_protocols. Distributed-system correctness arguments map to compiler_theory equivalence vocabulary: idempotency is referential transparency (multiple delivery same as one); eventual consistency is denotational equivalence in the limit; saga compensations are algebraic inverse operations.

concepts.name: monolith_vs_microservices
concepts.definition: Monolith: single deployable unit. Microservices: many small deployables, network-connected.
concepts.why: Different tradeoffs. Monolith: simpler deploy + local calls + atomic refactor. Microservices: independent scaling + tech diversity + team autonomy + network failure modes. Most modern systems are somewhere on the spectrum.

concepts.name: fallacies_of_distributed_computing
concepts.definition: Peter Deutsch's 8 fallacies: network is reliable, latency is zero, bandwidth is infinite, network is secure, topology doesn't change, one administrator, transport cost is zero, network is homogeneous.
concepts.why: Each false. Designing as if they're true produces fragile systems. Distributed code must explicitly handle: failures, latency, partial information, security, evolution.

concepts.name: service_mesh
concepts.definition: Infrastructure layer for service-to-service communication. Sidecar proxy per service + control plane. Istio, Linkerd, Consul Connect.
concepts.why: Standardise: mTLS, retry policy, circuit breaking, observability across all services without per-service code. Cost: complexity, sidecar resource overhead. Production-grade since ~2020.

concepts.name: sidecar_pattern
concepts.definition: Co-located helper process. App container + sidecar container in same pod. Sidecar handles cross-cutting concerns (TLS, telemetry).
concepts.why: Service mesh's deployment unit. Sidecar transparent to app. Cost: per-pod resource overhead. Alternative: shared libraries (per-language work).

concepts.name: API_gateway
concepts.definition: Single entry point for client requests. Handles auth, routing, rate limiting, transformation. Kong, AWS API Gateway, Tyk.
concepts.why: Centralise concerns for external traffic. Internal traffic via service mesh. Both patterns coexist in mature systems.

concepts.name: BFF_backend_for_frontend
concepts.definition: Per-client-type backend layer. Mobile BFF vs web BFF aggregate microservices per UI needs.
concepts.why: Avoids exposing internal microservices to clients. UI-specific data shaping. Common when different clients (web/mobile/IoT) need different data shapes.

concepts.name: circuit_breaker
concepts.definition: Wrap remote call. After N failures within window: open circuit; subsequent calls fail fast without attempting. After timeout: half-open (try one); close on success.
concepts.why: Prevent cascading failure: if downstream is dead, don't waste resources trying. Hystrix popularised; resilience4j, Polly modern implementations. Service mesh provides natively.

concepts.name: bulkhead_pattern
concepts.definition: Isolate failure domains. Separate thread pools / connection pools / instances per dependency or tenant.
concepts.why: Failure in one bulkhead doesn't sink others. Slow dependency consuming all threads = total outage; bulkheads contain. Ship's hull analogy.

concepts.name: retry_with_backoff
concepts.definition: Transient failure: wait + retry. Exponential backoff: 100ms, 200ms, 400ms, ... + jitter to avoid thundering herd.
concepts.why: Many failures are transient (load spike, brief partition). Retry recovers. Cost: amplifies load if downstream broken. Combined with circuit breaker.

concepts.name: jitter
concepts.definition: Random component added to backoff. Avoid synchronised retries from many clients.
concepts.why: Without jitter: clients retry at same instants → thundering herd → cause the next failure. Full jitter: random(0, backoff). Equal jitter: backoff/2 + random(0, backoff/2). Standard practice.

concepts.name: timeout_propagation
concepts.definition: Context-aware deadline. Request enters with deadline; passed through service calls; each call respects remaining budget.
concepts.why: Without: long downstream call leaves client thinking failed but work continues; resources wasted. With: cascading cancellation. gRPC's context.Deadline standard.

concepts.name: fail_fast_principle
concepts.definition: Detect failure early; don't continue degraded. Health check fail → remove from rotation; bad config → refuse to start.
concepts.why: Silent degradation is worst case (broken but appears healthy). Explicit failure is observable + recoverable. SRE practice.

concepts.name: graceful_degradation
concepts.definition: Reduce functionality under stress rather than fail entirely. Disable expensive features under load.
concepts.why: Partial service > no service. E.g., search works but personalization fallback to popular items. Designed-in vs reactive.

concepts.name: saga_pattern
concepts.definition: Sequence of local transactions with compensating transactions to undo on failure. Distributed transaction alternative to 2PC.
concepts.why: 2PC blocks; sagas don't. Long-running business processes. Cost: compensations are not always cleanly invertible (charged credit card, sent email). Modern: orchestration vs choreography flavours.

concepts.name: saga_choreography
concepts.definition: Each service reacts to events; emits own events. No central coordinator.
concepts.why: Decoupled but distributed logic; hard to reason about. Each service knows only its piece. Good for simple flows; debugging complex flows is hard.

concepts.name: saga_orchestration
concepts.definition: Central orchestrator drives saga. Calls services; on failure, calls compensations.
concepts.why: Centralised logic = easier to reason about. Cost: orchestrator is critical service. Tools: AWS Step Functions, Temporal, Camunda.

concepts.name: event_sourcing
concepts.definition: Persist sequence of events instead of current state. Current state = replay events.
concepts.why: Audit log built in. Time travel: reconstruct state at any point. Cost: query against current state requires projection. Used in financial systems, complex domains.

concepts.name: CQRS
concepts.definition: Command Query Responsibility Segregation. Separate write model (commands) from read model (queries).
concepts.why: Optimise each independently. Often paired with event sourcing. Write model = events; read models = projections for specific queries. Cost: eventual consistency between write + read.

concepts.name: two_phase_commit_2PC
concepts.definition: Distributed transaction protocol. Phase 1: prepare (all participants vote). Phase 2: commit or abort (coordinator decides).
concepts.why: ACID across multiple resources. Blocks indefinitely if coordinator fails after prepare. Used in XA transactions; modern systems prefer sagas + idempotency.

concepts.name: TCC_try_confirm_cancel
concepts.definition: Three-phase pattern. Try: reserve resources. Confirm: commit. Cancel: release reservations.
concepts.why: Saga variant with explicit reservation phase. Better than 2PC (no blocking) but requires application-level support. Used in payment + booking systems.

concepts.name: idempotency_distributed
concepts.definition: Operation produces same result regardless of how many times executed. Tied to idempotency key.
concepts.why: Necessary for at-least-once delivery + safe retries. Client sends key; server detects duplicate. Stripe's API exemplar.

concepts.name: exactly_once_semantics
concepts.definition: Each operation executes exactly once despite failures. Hard in general; achievable with constraints.
concepts.why: Idempotency + at-least-once = effectively-once. Pure exactly-once impossible without coordination. Kafka's 'exactly once' is producer idempotency + transactional offsets.

concepts.name: at_most_once_delivery
concepts.definition: Message delivered zero or one times. Lost messages possible; duplicates not.
concepts.why: Default for fire-and-forget (UDP). Use case: metrics, telemetry where loss acceptable.

concepts.name: at_least_once_delivery
concepts.definition: Message delivered one or more times. Duplicates possible; loss not.
concepts.why: Default for most reliable messaging (Kafka, SQS). Requires idempotent consumers. Most common production choice.

concepts.name: lamport_timestamp
concepts.definition: Logical clock: increment on local event, max(local, received)+1 on receive. Defines partial order.
concepts.why: Distributed system has no global time. Lamport timestamps order causally-related events. Cannot detect concurrency. Foundation of distributed time.

concepts.name: vector_clock
concepts.definition: Each node has counter; on send, includes whole vector; on receive, max element-wise + increment own.
concepts.why: Captures causality + concurrency (vectors incomparable = concurrent events). More info than Lamport at cost of size O(N) nodes. Used in Dynamo, Voldemort.

concepts.name: hybrid_logical_clock
concepts.definition: HLC. Combine physical time + logical counter. Bounded drift from physical clock.
concepts.why: Lamport doesn't relate to wall clock. HLC: physical time-ish + logical for tie-breaking. Used in CockroachDB, YugabyteDB. Practical compromise.

concepts.name: NTP_clock_sync
concepts.definition: Network Time Protocol. Synchronise clocks via stratum hierarchy. Typical drift ~1-50ms.
concepts.why: Best-effort wall-clock sync. Insufficient for ordering events (clocks drift). Spanner uses TrueTime (atomic clocks + GPS) for tight bounds; few systems can.

concepts.name: TrueTime_Spanner
concepts.definition: Google Spanner's bounded-uncertainty clock API. Returns interval [earliest, latest] with bounded uncertainty.
concepts.why: Tight bounds (~7ms uncertainty) via GPS + atomic clocks. Enables external consistency. Other systems (CockroachDB) emulate with HLC + larger uncertainty.

concepts.name: heartbeat_failure_detection
concepts.definition: Periodic 'I'm alive' message. Receiver suspects failure after N missed.
concepts.why: Simple. Threshold tradeoff: too tight = false positives; too loose = slow detection. Most basic failure detector.

concepts.name: gossip_protocol
concepts.definition: Each node periodically gossips state to random peers. State spreads exponentially.
concepts.why: Scalable failure detection + state dissemination. O(log N) rounds to converge. Used in Cassandra, Consul, Dynamo.

concepts.name: phi_accrual_failure_detector
concepts.definition: Continuous probability of failure rather than binary up/down. φ value rises as heartbeats overdue.
concepts.why: Better than threshold-based: app decides what φ level triggers action. Used in Cassandra, Akka. Adapts to network latency variability.

concepts.name: SWIM_protocol
concepts.definition: Scalable Weakly-consistent Infection-style process group Membership. Direct probe + indirect probe via peers.
concepts.why: Used in Hashicorp Serf, Memberlist, Consul. Better failure detection accuracy than naive heartbeat. Subgossiping spreads membership info.

concepts.name: service_discovery
concepts.definition: Mechanism for services to find each other. DNS-based (Kubernetes), key-value (Consul, etcd), registry (Eureka).
concepts.why: Hardcoded endpoints don't survive scaling/restart/migration. Discovery dynamic. K8s DNS-based standard for Kubernetes; service mesh extends.

concepts.name: load_balancer_L4
concepts.definition: Layer 4 (TCP) load balancing. Distribute connections; no payload inspection.
concepts.why: Fast, simple, protocol-agnostic. Used for high throughput. Cost: can't route based on HTTP headers, URL. AWS NLB, Linux IPVS.

concepts.name: load_balancer_L7
concepts.definition: Layer 7 (HTTP) load balancing. Inspect headers, route by path/host/header. SSL termination.
concepts.why: Smart routing: canary deploys, A/B tests, version pinning. Envoy, Nginx, HAProxy, AWS ALB. Slower than L4; functionality justifies.

concepts.name: consistent_hashing_distributed
concepts.definition: Hash ring distributes load. Adding/removing nodes moves O(1/N) keys.
concepts.why: Already in databases_and_storage; here as distributed system pattern. Foundation of distributed caches, load balancers, sharded systems.

concepts.name: sticky_session
concepts.definition: Load balancer routes same client to same backend. Cookie-based or IP-based.
concepts.why: When backend has session state. Cost: uneven load, dies with backend. Modern: prefer stateless backends + shared session store (Redis).

concepts.name: liveness_probe
concepts.definition: Periodic 'is this instance healthy enough to keep running?' check. Failure → restart.
concepts.why: K8s standard. Catches deadlocks, deep failures. Cost: aggressive probe = restart loops. Tune to actual recovery time.

concepts.name: readiness_probe
concepts.definition: 'Is this instance ready to serve traffic?' check. Failure → remove from load balancer (don't restart).
concepts.why: Slow startup (cache warm-up, DB connection). Without readiness: traffic routed before ready → errors. K8s readiness gates LB.

concepts.name: graceful_shutdown
concepts.definition: On shutdown signal: stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight, then exit.
concepts.why: Abrupt shutdown = in-flight requests fail. Graceful: K8s sends SIGTERM, waits terminationGracePeriodSeconds, then SIGKILL. Standard pattern.

concepts.name: rate_limiting_token_bucket
concepts.definition: Token bucket: tokens added at rate R, max capacity C. Each request consumes a token; reject if empty.
concepts.why: Allows bursts (up to C) while limiting sustained rate (R). Standard algorithm. Used in API gateways, load balancers.

concepts.name: rate_limiting_leaky_bucket
concepts.definition: Leaky bucket: incoming requests queue; processed at constant rate. Overflow = drop.
concepts.why: Smooths output (vs token bucket allowing bursts). Used where downstream can't handle bursts. Different tradeoffs from token bucket.

concepts.name: distributed_rate_limiting
concepts.definition: Rate limit across cluster of API gateways. Redis-based counter + atomic INCR + TTL.
concepts.why: Local rate limit per node lets cluster exceed global limit by N. Centralised counter expensive. Compromise: distributed approximations (Redis cell, sliding window log).

concepts.name: backpressure
concepts.definition: Downstream signals 'slow down' to upstream. Bounded queues; refuse work when full.
concepts.why: Without: queue grows unboundedly, memory exhaustion, cascading failure. With: caller deals with rejection (retry, drop, alternate path). Reactive streams' core principle.

concepts.name: distributed_locking_Redlock
concepts.definition: Redlock algorithm: lock acquired on majority of N Redis instances. Antirez 2016.
concepts.why: Popular pattern. Controversial: Kleppmann argues unsafe for protecting state. Safer use: advisory locks (efficiency, not correctness). Use ZooKeeper/etcd for safety-critical.

concepts.name: distributed_tracing
concepts.definition: Track requests as they flow through services. Each service adds span; spans assembled into trace.
concepts.why: Debug performance, follow request paths. OpenTelemetry standard. Jaeger, Tempo, Zipkin backends. Critical for microservices observability.

concepts.name: trace_context_propagation
concepts.definition: Trace ID + span ID + sampling decision passed in headers. W3C Trace Context standard.
concepts.why: Without propagation, can't connect spans across services. Standard headers: traceparent, tracestate. Frameworks auto-propagate.

concepts.name: structured_logging
concepts.definition: Logs as key-value records (JSON), not free-form text. Searchable + filterable.
concepts.why: Grep on text doesn't scale. Structured: query by user_id, request_id, level. Modern: include trace_id for cross-system correlation. Loki, Elasticsearch, CloudWatch query.

concepts.name: metrics_prometheus_style
concepts.definition: Time-series numeric measurements. Counter, gauge, histogram. Scraped or pushed.
concepts.why: Aggregate behaviour at scale. Logs answer 'what happened to this request'; metrics answer 'how is the system overall'. Prometheus + Grafana standard.

concepts.name: three_pillars_observability
concepts.definition: Logs (events), metrics (numbers), traces (causal chains). Distinct but complementary.
concepts.why: Each answers different questions. Modern observability stacks integrate all three. OpenTelemetry unifying API. Tempo + Loki + Mimir (Grafana) example stack.

concepts.name: SLO
concepts.definition: Service Level Objective. Target reliability (99.9% availability, p99 < 200ms). Measured over rolling window.
concepts.why: Quantitative reliability goal. Not 100% (cost-prohibitive). Drives engineering priorities. Google SRE book popularised.

concepts.name: SLA
concepts.definition: Service Level Agreement. Contractual reliability commitment with penalties. SLO is internal target; SLA is external promise.
concepts.why: SLA typically looser than SLO (buffer). SLO breach = engineering action; SLA breach = legal action. Distinction matters.

concepts.name: SLI
concepts.definition: Service Level Indicator. Measured metric backing the SLO. e.g. successful_requests / total_requests.
concepts.why: SLO needs measurement. SLI = the measurement. Common SLIs: availability, latency, throughput, error rate. Choose carefully — what you measure becomes what you optimise.

concepts.name: error_budget
concepts.definition: 1 - SLO = allowed unreliability. 99.9% SLO = 0.1% error budget = ~43 minutes/month.
concepts.why: Quantifies risk tolerance. Spent budget = freeze risky changes. Unused = OK to ship faster. Aligns SRE + dev incentives.

concepts.name: RED_method
concepts.definition: Rate, Errors, Duration. Three metrics per service. Tom Wilkie's framework.
concepts.why: Simple per-service dashboard. Rate: requests/sec. Errors: % failed. Duration: latency distribution. Good for request-driven services.

concepts.name: USE_method
concepts.definition: Utilization, Saturation, Errors. Per resource (CPU, disk, network). Brendan Gregg.
concepts.why: Resource-centric view. Complementary to RED (per-service). Both used together for full picture.

concepts.name: chaos_engineering
concepts.definition: Deliberately inject failures in production. Verify system handles. Netflix Chaos Monkey originated.
concepts.why: Reveal hidden failure modes before they happen organically. Discipline: run experiments, observe, fix, repeat. Mature SRE practice.

concepts.name: blast_radius_limitation
concepts.definition: Scope of impact when something goes wrong. Cells, canaries, gradual rollouts limit.
concepts.why: Bad deploy to 100% = total outage. Cells (subset of traffic) → blast radius bounded. Standard production safety.

concepts.name: canary_deployment
concepts.definition: Roll out new version to small subset (5%). Monitor metrics. Expand or roll back.
concepts.why: Limit blast radius of bad code. Catches issues affecting real traffic. Standard rollout pattern. Service mesh + LB support.

concepts.name: blue_green_deployment
concepts.definition: Two identical environments. Switch traffic from blue to green atomically. Roll back by switching back.
concepts.why: Zero-downtime + fast rollback. Cost: double resources during deploy. Less granular than canary (all-or-nothing).

concepts.name: feature_flag
concepts.definition: Runtime toggle to enable/disable code path. LaunchDarkly, Unleash, GrowthBook.
concepts.why: Decouple deploy from release. Test in production safely. Rollback without redeploy. Trunk-based development enabler.

concepts.name: blameless_postmortem
concepts.definition: Incident analysis focused on systems + processes, not individual fault. Document timeline + root cause + actions.
concepts.why: Fear of blame hides information. Blameless = honesty + better lessons. Google SRE + Etsy popularised. Standard mature engineering practice.

concepts.name: distributed_cache_pattern
concepts.definition: Shared cache across application instances. Reduce DB load + cross-service computation.
concepts.why: Redis, Memcached. Patterns: cache-aside (app manages), write-through (cache transparent to app), write-behind (async write to DB).

concepts.name: cache_aside_pattern
concepts.definition: App reads cache; on miss reads DB + populates cache. Writes invalidate cache.
concepts.why: Simple. App controls when to cache. Cost: race conditions on invalidation. Standard caching pattern.

concepts.name: write_through_cache
concepts.definition: Writes go to cache + DB synchronously. Cache always consistent with DB.
concepts.why: Read consistency guarantee. Cost: write latency = both stores. Used where read-after-write matters.

concepts.name: write_behind_cache
concepts.definition: Writes to cache; async flush to DB. Lower write latency, possible loss on cache failure.
concepts.why: Throughput at cost of durability. Used for non-critical writes (analytics, logs). Background flush controls DB load.

concepts.name: cache_invalidation_problem
concepts.definition: 'There are only two hard things in CS: cache invalidation, naming things, and off-by-one errors.' Phil Karlton.
concepts.why: Stale cache = wrong data. TTL is approximate. Event-based invalidation is complex. Pragmatic: short TTL + accept some staleness.

concepts.name: CDN_edge_caching
concepts.definition: Cache at network edge (close to users). CloudFront, Cloudflare, Fastly.
concepts.why: Reduce latency + origin load. Static assets default. Increasingly dynamic content cached at edge with custom logic (Cloudflare Workers).

concepts.name: geo_replication
concepts.definition: Replicate data + services across regions. Primary-replica or active-active.
concepts.why: Locality (lower latency for distant users) + DR (region failure tolerance). Cost: cross-region replication latency, conflict resolution if active-active.

concepts.name: multi_region_failover
concepts.definition: Failover from primary region to secondary on region failure. DNS-based (Route 53), application-level.
concepts.why: Cloud region failures happen (AWS US-EAST-1 multiple times). Multi-region serves availability. Cost: complexity + replication cost.

concepts.name: anycast_routing
concepts.definition: Same IP announced from multiple locations. BGP routes traffic to nearest.
concepts.why: Global load distribution + DDoS mitigation. Cloudflare, Google DNS use heavily. Network-level optimization invisible to apps.

concepts.name: DNS_based_load_balancing
concepts.definition: DNS returns different IPs based on geography, health, weights. Route 53 traffic policies, Cloudflare DNS.
concepts.why: Coarse-grained (DNS TTL caching) but global. Often combined with anycast + L7 LB. Different layer of load distribution.

concepts.name: horizontal_vs_vertical_scaling
concepts.definition: Horizontal: add more instances. Vertical: bigger instance.
concepts.why: Vertical has limits + single point of failure. Horizontal scales further + fault tolerant. Vertical simpler. Modern: horizontal preferred when possible.

concepts.name: stateless_design
concepts.definition: Service holds no client state between requests. State in DB / cache / token.
concepts.why: Enables horizontal scaling: any instance handles any request. Loss of instance loses nothing. Auto-scaling friendly. Foundation of modern microservices.

concepts.name: messaging_queue_pattern
concepts.definition: Producer → queue → consumer. Decouple time + load. Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS.
concepts.why: Async processing. Bursts absorbed by queue. Consumer can be slower than producer temporarily. Foundation of event-driven architecture.

concepts.name: pub_sub_pattern
concepts.definition: Publishers send to topic; multiple subscribers receive. Decoupled.
concepts.why: Fan-out. Many consumers for same event. Kafka topics, RabbitMQ exchanges, Redis pub/sub. Common for event-driven systems.

concepts.name: dead_letter_queue
concepts.definition: Messages that consumers can't process moved to DLQ. Investigate without blocking main queue.
concepts.why: Poison message blocks queue if retried forever. DLQ separates. Manual triage or automated processing. Standard pattern.

rules.name: circuit_breaker_prevents_cascading_failure
then: circuit breaker prevents wasted work + caller can fail fast
rules.why: Without: keep trying, threads blocked waiting, eventually thread pool exhausted, cascading outage. With: open circuit fails immediately, threads return, system stable. Standard resilience pattern.

rules.name: idempotency_required_for_at_least_once
then: consumer must be idempotent
rules.why: At-least-once: duplicates expected. Non-idempotent consumer: duplicate = wrong state (charged twice, sent twice). Idempotency key + check enables safe retries. Kafka + SQS systems live here.

rules.name: exactly_once_via_idempotency_at_least_once
if: consumer is idempotent + delivery is at-least-once
then: effective semantics is exactly-once
rules.why: Pure exactly-once impossible. Idempotency reduces to: 'do the work; duplicate doesn't matter'. Effectively exactly-once from observer's view. Modern Kafka, Stripe's API exemplify.

rules.name: jitter_prevents_thundering_herd
if: many clients retry with deterministic backoff
then: retries synchronise + amplify load
rules.why: All clients hit 'wait 1s, try again' simultaneously. Add random jitter → spread retries → smoother load. Standard. AWS exponential backoff doc recommends.

rules.name: timeout_propagation_avoids_wasted_work
if: request deadlines propagate through service calls
then: downstream stops work when client gave up
rules.why: Without: client times out at 1s; downstream continues for 5s; resources wasted. With: each call checks remaining budget. gRPC context standard. Critical for high-throughput systems.

rules.name: graceful_shutdown_required_for_zero_downtime
if: service handles in-flight requests on shutdown
then: rolling deploys can be zero-downtime
rules.why: Without: SIGTERM kills in-flight requests; clients see errors. With: stop accepting + drain + exit. K8s + LB combine: deregister from LB → wait → SIGTERM → wait → SIGKILL.

rules.name: saga_replaces_2PC_for_long_processes
if: transaction spans services + cannot block for hours
then: saga pattern outperforms 2PC
rules.why: 2PC blocks during prepare-commit. Long-running business processes can't lock for hours. Saga: per-step + compensations. Cost: not truly atomic; failure cases more complex.

rules.name: event_sourcing_preserves_history
then: audit log + time travel come free
rules.why: Current state is a derived view. Events are source of truth. Replay to any point: 'what was state on Friday?'. Cost: queries against current state need projections. Foundation in financial + regulated systems.

rules.name: CQRS_decouples_read_write_optimisation
if: read patterns differ significantly from write
then: separate read + write models outperform unified
rules.why: Single model serves both: compromises on both. Separate: writes optimised for consistency; reads optimised for query patterns (denormalised, multi-table joins precomputed). Cost: eventual consistency between models.

rules.name: vector_clocks_capture_concurrency
then: concurrent vs causal relationships are detectable
rules.why: Lamport timestamps order but lose concurrency (everything appears ordered). Vector clocks: incomparable vectors = concurrent. Necessary for conflict detection in eventually-consistent systems.

rules.name: physical_clocks_unreliable_for_ordering
if: events ordered by wall clock timestamps
then: clock skew breaks ordering
rules.why: NTP has ms-level drift; events within window have wrong relative order. Use logical time (Lamport, vector, HLC) for causal ordering. Wall clock acceptable only with TrueTime-style bounded uncertainty.

rules.name: gossip_scales_to_huge_clusters
if: membership + state must propagate across thousands of nodes
then: gossip protocol outperforms broadcast
rules.why: Broadcast: O(N) per update; gossip: O(log N) rounds to converge, O(1) per node per round. Cassandra: 1000s of nodes via gossip. Eventually consistent state.

rules.name: Redlock_unsafe_for_correctness_critical_locking
then: Redlock is not safe enough
rules.why: Kleppmann's critique: process pause + clock skew can violate mutual exclusion. Acceptable for advisory locks (efficiency). For correctness, use Raft-based (etcd, ZooKeeper) with fencing tokens.

rules.name: trace_context_required_for_microservice_debugging
then: distributed tracing is required to understand behaviour
rules.why: Single-server: stack trace shows everything. Microservices: each service is a stack trace. Trace context links them. OpenTelemetry standardising. Critical for production microservices.

rules.name: structured_logs_correlate_via_request_id
if: logs include request ID propagated across services
then: full request flow is queryable
rules.why: Free-form logs: grep + hope. Structured + request ID: query 'all logs for request X across all services'. Foundation of microservice debugging.

rules.name: SLO_drives_engineering_priority
then: risky changes are blocked until reliability improves
rules.why: Error budget left → ship faster. Budget spent → focus on reliability. Aligns dev (ship features) + SRE (preserve reliability) incentives via shared metric. Google SRE practice.

rules.name: canary_limits_blast_radius
then: bad code affects 5% of traffic before being caught
rules.why: Vs. full deploy: bad code affects 100%. Cost: deploy slower. Modern: automated canary analysis (Spinnaker, Argo Rollouts) detects regressions + rolls back automatically.

rules.name: chaos_engineering_reveals_hidden_failures
then: latent failure modes surface before causing outages
rules.why: Production has failure modes test environments don't. Chaos Monkey (Netflix): kill instances. Failure simulation reveals: missing timeouts, unbounded retries, untested fallbacks. SRE practice.

rules.name: cache_aside_simple_but_races_possible
then: concurrent writes can produce stale cache
rules.why: Two clients: A reads (miss), A reads DB, [B writes DB + invalidates cache], A populates cache with old value. Cache stale until next invalidation. Standard race; mitigations: short TTL, double-check, distributed locks.

rules.name: anycast_routes_to_nearest_PoP
if: service announces same IP from multiple PoPs
then: BGP routes traffic to nearest PoP
rules.why: Network-level load balancing + latency optimisation. Cloudflare global DNS: 1.1.1.1 anycast across 300+ cities. Each user → nearest. Failure: BGP withdraws + reroutes.

rules.name: stateless_services_horizontally_scalable
then: any instance can serve any request
rules.why: State elsewhere (DB, cache, JWT). Add/remove instances freely. Auto-scaling works naturally. Load balancing simple (no sticky sessions). Foundation of cloud-native.

rules.name: dead_letter_queue_isolates_poison_messages
then: DLQ prevents it from blocking the main queue
rules.why: Without DLQ: retry forever, queue stuck. With DLQ: after N retries, move to DLQ for investigation. Main queue continues. Standard messaging pattern (SQS, Kafka with retry topics).
